name: Diffie–Hellman public-key distribution
description: A published method and framework for establishing shared keying information over a public communication channel.

impact.note: Key agreement runs unseen in a large share of secure connections; it gave strangers a way to share secrets openly, and public-key cryptography grew from it.

date.basis: Date in the cited source; see scope and caveats.

events.statement: Diffie and Hellman published a possible public-key distribution method and described public-key encryption as a distinct open problem.

evidence.supports: The authors set out public-key distribution and cite partial NSF support.

events.caveats: A theoretical publication, not evidence of an operating secure public service; independent classified work is not assessed.
